proof_attempt_summary: The D-stage graph closes the finite-roster timing recursion and support theorem, a target-pair ternary overlap construction, and sharp binary and fixed-floor tier frontiers for a structured last-FIFO batch family. Two panel defects were repaired, the graph passed fsck with no open statements, and the closest-source comparison was added. tldr: In a fixed scarce-service roster, independent randomized priority labels induce each applicant's first-service date through shared FIFO capacity. Conditioning on the tagged tier turns every other applicant into an independent Bernoulli blocker, yielding an exact polynomial-time timing law and an if-and-only-if busy-period support theorem. Two full-support tiers attain every feasible date, but on the last-FIFO batch family their best early-versus-late overlap satisfies \(\sup_p\omega_i\sim\sqrt m\,2^{-m}\) for \(m=n-1\); three unfloored tiers instead give both target dates mass above \(3/8\) and have fixed-pair supremum \(1/2\). With a fixed operational floor, binary overlap is asymptotic to \((1-\eta)\sqrt m\,2^{-m}\), while every fixed feasible \(K\ge3\) has overlap asymptotic to \(\{1-(K-1)\eta\}(1-\eta)^m\). For every fixed \(0<\eta\le1/3\), three tiers are uniquely asymptotically optimal: binary overlap is negligible relative to ternary overlap, and each additional feasible fixed tier keeps base \(1-\eta\) but strictly lowers the leading constant. The exact timing law and support apply conditionally to a realized anchor roster when \(p_{ik}=\theta_k(X_i)\); the target-specific row design class and the growing-horizon batch frontier are finite-roster conditional extensions, not anchor-policy or anchor-asymptotic theorems.
gap: Aronow and Samii's general exposure workflow uses known exposure probabilities in inverse-probability estimators, but it neither derives queue-induced service-date probabilities nor asserts that positivity alone is adequate. Existing priority-queue experiments analyze terminal receipt, while transient queue theory does not choose randomized tier designs or certify a minimal tier count for two specified dates.
fill: The blocker recursion supplies exact propensities; the busy-period theorem supplies necessary-and-sufficient support; the binary converse shows that positive date support can coexist with exponentially vanishing overlap; and the explicit rational nested-witness construction proves that a third tier guarantees constant overlap.
